observation_summary: The JsonParserSequence skips a token when switching to a new parser if that parser already has a current token, leading to incorrect parsing results.
hypothesis: The nextToken() method in JsonParserSequence incorrectly assumes that it must always call nextToken() on the delegate parser when switching, failing to account for cases where the delegate already has a valid current token that should be returned instead.
prediction: The fix will introduce a state variable to track whether the next token should be suppressed and modify the nextToken() logic to check for existing tokens before calling nextToken() on the delegate.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the introduction of a boolean flag '_suppressNextToken' and a modification to the nextToken() method to check for existing tokens (delegate.hasCurrentToken()) during the switch, confirming that the original algorithm for token retrieval was flawed.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in how the parser sequence manages token retrieval during parser switching. It is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), but a fundamental flaw in the iteration/retrieval logic of the sequence parser, which is best classified as an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The fix diff introduces a new state variable '_suppressNextToken'.
The fix diff modifies the nextToken() method to check for existing tokens using 'delegate.hasCurrentToken()' instead of unconditionally calling 'delegate.nextToken()'.
The bug report states that the sequence skips a token on a switched parser.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check, the core issue is the incorrect implementation of the token retrieval algorithm, not just a missing validation guard.
The fix involves more than just initializing a value; it changes the entire control flow logic of the nextToken() method.
